title: Stem stitch
subtitle: The standard outline stitch for curves and fine lines
excerpt: Stem stitch builds a smooth twisted outline by working overlapping angled stitches along any drawn line. Once the rhythm is set, curves follow naturally. It is the foundation outline stitch of surface embroidery.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), outline stitches chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), stem stitch entry.

glossaryTerms.definition: The strand in the needle that you are actively stitching with.
The drawn or traced line on the fabric that guides where the stitches go.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands for fine lines, 3 strands for bolder outlines

content.text: Draw a curved line on your fabric with a water-soluble pen. Bring the needle up at the left end of the line (point A).
Insert the needle a stitch-length ahead (point B) and bring it up halfway back at the midpoint (point C). Keep the thread below the needle.
Pull through. For the next stitch, insert a full stitch-length ahead of B and bring up at B.
Continue along the line, keeping the thread consistently on the same side of the needle throughout.

items.symptom: The line looks bumpy rather than smooth
items.cause: Thread is switching sides between stitches.
items.fix: Choose above or below at the first stitch and hold it there consistently throughout.

items.cause: Stitch length too long for the curve radius.
items.fix: Shorten the stitch length on tight curves. Smaller stitches follow the curve more accurately.

content.text: Stem stitch is the primary outline stitch for floral embroidery, crewelwork stems, and monogram outlines. It also works as a dense fill when rows are packed side by side.
